name: stackup-from-pdf-report
prompt: model this substrate from the pdf

inputs.notes: A synthetic Tamsworth Interconnect Co. stackup report, Rev C, as a PDF (fictional fabricator and products): 8 copper layers, 4 vias, 5 controlled impedance rows, fab rules and capability limits.

notes: For whoever reads the grader's output, not for the runner. Whoever launches the runner stages only `inputs` (the PDF) and must not expose evals/checks to it: the grader-side CSV twin under evals/checks/testdata/case_b/ holds the answers, including the values the PDF leaves out. The twin is the PDF in the fab-report SECTION layout, so substrate_grader.py and grade_pdf_report.py can read it; evals/checks/make_pdf_report.py renders the PDF from it (with PyMuPDF, outside the grader's environment), and test_grade_pdf_report.py checks with pdftotext that the PDF states every value the graders compare and none of the hidden ones. The PDF's traps, each graded against the twin: mil declared controlling, with the L4-L5 prepreg's mm cell reading 0.1000 against its 4.00 mil (the twin holds 0.1016); inner copper as 1 oz only (the twin holds 0.0350 mm, the figure SKILL.md gives for 1 oz, so a runner that converts 1 oz otherwise goes red on the copper rows and the totals); the L5-L6 core with no thickness and the finished total given (the twin holds the 1.1362 mm that balances it, so the totals reconcile by construction and a judge assertion asks that the reconciliation be reported as not performed); L1 referenced to L3 across a voided L2; BD-1 listed as drilled L1 to L8 and backdrilled from L8 keeping L1 to L4 (coded as a via stopping at L4, backdrilled from the bottom); SV-1 a stacked L1 to L3 microvia; TH-1 with non-functional pads reduced on L2 to L7; the aspect-ratio depth basis only in a footnote under the via table and no statement that limits are inclusive, with TH-1 exactly on the 10:1 mechanical limit; capability limits in mil, inches, ratios and counts; and Rev C enlarging UV-1's pad while the via table still shows the Rev B annular ring. The commands run from the repository root. Whoever launches the runner passes runner_artifacts to it verbatim, with the prompt; no script reads it. Judges get <output>/board.py, <output>/RESTATEMENT.md, <output>/COMPLETION.md, the PDF and the CSV twin, each as --artifact; the twin lets a judge tell a value the report backs from an invented one. RESTATEMENT.md shows what the restatement said, not when it was given: a judge can see its content, not that it preceded the code. The self-tests of both graders run with `python -m pytest -q skills/jitx-substrate-modeler` from the repository root; run them after any edit to a grader, the twin or the PDF.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write the substrate to exactly <output>/board.py, the restatement of the report it gives the user before writing any code to <output>/RESTATEMENT.md, and its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A restatement of the report before any code: 8 copper layers, the 17-row stack, Dk/Df at 2.0 GHz, foil weights and Rz, the 4 vias, the 5 controlled rows and the fab rules, flagging that the L5-L6 core has no stated thickness, that inner copper is given only as 1 oz, that the L4-L5 prepreg's mm cell disagrees with its controlling mil value, and that the report does not say whether limits are inclusive. Then a single-file substrate (board.py) whose every value traces to the report: an explicit 8-layer Stackup of 17 entries in mm converted from mil, with the L4-L5 prepreg at 0.1016 mm, inner copper at the skill's 0.035 mm for 1 oz and the L5-L6 core solved from the 80.00 mil finished thickness (1.1362 mm), each named as derived; one material class per material, with material_name carrying the product; UV-1 with the Rev C 10.0 mil pad and its annular ring re-derived as 3.0 mil, SV-1 as one laser via from L1 to L3, BD-1 as a mechanical via from L1 stopping at L4 with a bottom backdrill of the four stated dimensions, TH-1 with diameters giving ViaDiameter(nfp=0.2794) on L2 to L7; the 19 mappable fab rules, with min_drill_diameter holding the 4.0 mil laser minimum, the board maximums converted from inches, and the capability limits that are not lengths (both aspect ratios, the stacked-level count) in the rules class docstring rather than as attributes; SE-50 on L1, L4 and L8 and DIFF-100 on L4 and L8 with velocity from Eps_eff and the L1 reference on L3 at 3x the 0.1524 mm of dielectric between them; STANDARD documented but not modelled; and the completeness check block with the Stackup reconciliation reported as not performed, since the core was solved for the total, and the unstated core and the inclusive-limit question as open items.

assertions.text: generated file type-checks against the installed jitx package

the substrate in board.py matches the report row for row against the grader-side CSV twin: stackup in controlling-mil values, materials and names, vias and drill direction, fab rules, routing structures and reference planes

ruff format leaves every labeled derivation in board.py whole, on the line with its label, and no label sits on a bracket whose entries carry no label of their own (the judges read the unformatted file)

BD-1 is backdrilled from the bottom and stops at L4 with the stated backdrill dimensions, SV-1 is one laser via from L1 to L3, TH-1 has its non-functional pads on L2 to L7 only, L1 references L3 at 3x the dielectric between them, and the capability limits that are not lengths are documented in the rules class docstring, not set as attributes

no invented numbers: every value in board.py that no report cell backs (the reference-plane widths, the unstated L5-L6 core thickness, the inner copper thickness from its oz weight, and anything else) is labeled at its call site with where it came from: a skill default naming its rule, or a derivation from stated report values

the L5-L6 core's unstated thickness is named as an open item, and the completeness check's Stackup row reports the thickness reconciliation as not performed (or equivalent), since that thickness was solved from the stated total rather than checked against it

RESTATEMENT.md restates the report (layer count and construction, Dk/Df and their frequency, foil weights and Rz, the via inventory, impedance targets, fab rules) and flags the unstated core thickness, the oz-only inner copper and the L4-L5 prepreg's disagreeing mm cell
UV-1's annular ring is re-derived from the Rev C 10.0 mil pad as 3.0 mil (0.0762 mm), not taken from the via table's 2.5 mil, which predates Rev C

TH-1's 10.00:1 aspect ratio, exactly on the 10:1 limit in a report that does not say whether its limits are inclusive, is not reported as a violation: it is either asked about or recorded as an open item that names the convention assumed
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows
